title: What lobbyists asked for, by kind
question: What do lobbyists ask officials for: laws, permits, contracts, pension investments or appointments, and how much of it can be tied to a decision on record?
finding: Of 66,677 reported contacts, 36,045 concern planning or building approval for a project and 13,008 other, or general discussion. Lobbyists sought approval or support in 54.9% of contacts and opposed something in 2.6%; the rest say “monitor”, ask for changes or give no position. Only 2,291 contacts (3.4%) carry a Board file number that matches a file on record, covering 294 files; a further 250 can be tied to 36 enacted ordinances by the words of their subject.
how: Each contact is sorted by its department, subject area, issue and outcome sought, using fixed word lists (pension investments by department; legislation by a file number or words such as ordinance, code, tax; appointments; contracts, grants and leases; planning and building approvals). The position is read from the “outcome sought” text. Board files are matched as described in the next two screens.
limits: Lobbying is registered, and so is giving by a lobbyist’s clients and colleagues. The categories are read from short free text that lobbyists type in their own words, so some contacts are misfiled, and “monitor” often hides a position. Planning cases, permits and pension investments are decided by commissions and staff whose votes and decisions are not in the Board’s files; lobbied Planning Commission projects are in the site’s “Votes, appeals and hearings” page (screen lobbied-projects) and permit consultants in the site’s “How the permit process works” page. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
